claim: Seven local failure/repair lessons from three original studies; no independent transfer claim.

lessons.title: Identity cue consumes the main mass
lessons.origin: Observed authoring revision; original art made in this session
lessons.observed: A broad lantern and gallery consume the short tower.
lessons.cause: Too many of the sixteen rows belong to the cap.
lessons.intervention: Reduce lantern width and gallery height; give the shaft more rows.
lessons.preserve: Keep the lamp as the brightest cue and its support on the shaft.
lessons.limit: The final shaft is still irregular. A taller shaft alone does not establish convincing masonry.
lessons.probe: At native size, read the whole structure before its lamp.

lessons.title: A one-cell bridge closes a needed opening
lessons.origin: Observed authoring revision; original art made in this session
lessons.observed: The crown closes the small opening beside the bent trunk.
lessons.cause: A connecting cell links two masses that need a visible gap.
lessons.intervention: Cut the planned notch through the responsible crown mask.
lessons.preserve: Keep the trunk attached to the main crown and rooted below.
lessons.limit: A clear rectangle diagnoses this chosen gap; it is not a rule that tree foliage must be disconnected.
lessons.probe: Hide surface color and check the chosen negative space.

lessons.title: Shadow becomes a hollow dome
lessons.origin: Observed authoring revision; original art made in this session
lessons.observed: The large uniform lower-right dark patch reads like a hollow shell.
lessons.cause: Shadow follows a horizontal band instead of the crown turning away from light.
lessons.intervention: Rebuild the shadow along the lower-right turning edge.
lessons.preserve: Keep the wind gesture, broad lobes and trunk opening.
lessons.limit: The remaining leaf marks still step across the crown. This repair addresses volume, not finished foliage.
lessons.probe: Compare the light and dark masses before viewing tiny leaf marks.

lessons.title: An added patch preserves the wrong boundary
lessons.origin: Observed authoring revision; original art made in this session
lessons.observed: A restored midtone patch remains enclosed by a dark ring.
lessons.cause: Adding light inside the old shadow retains its misleading contour.
lessons.intervention: Remove the ring and redraw the shadow boundary instead of adding another patch.
lessons.limit: This is a rejected repair from the same tree, not an extra independent experiment.
lessons.probe: Judge the revised piece alone: does the canopy still look hollow?

lessons.title: Ground hides all actor silhouettes
lessons.origin: Observed authoring revision; original art made in this session
lessons.observed: The filled ground makes a nearly solid silhouette view.
lessons.cause: Environment and actors are treated as one foreground mass.
lessons.intervention: Dim declared environment parts in the diagnostic silhouette view.
lessons.preserve: Preserve paint order and occlusion; the color artwork is not improved by this display change.
lessons.limit: A better diagnostic is not a better pose. Hidden actor parts remain hidden.
lessons.probe: Inspect the gaps between bodies and equipment, then return to color.

lessons.title: Feet fall past the supporting deck
lessons.origin: Observed authoring revision; original art made in this session
lessons.observed: The skeleton feet extend below the near bridge boundary.
lessons.cause: The contact points were not checked against the support surface.
lessons.intervention: Redraw the deck boundary and check sole anchors inside it, excluding the front rim.
lessons.preserve: Keep the forward skeleton gesture and separation of its legs.
lessons.limit: An inside-mask check cannot infer gravity, balance or perspective. It tests only the declared point.
lessons.probe: Read the contact in the complete scene as well as in this crop.

lessons.title: Parallel weapons confuse the exchange
lessons.origin: Observed authoring revision; original art made in this session
lessons.observed: Two nearby diagonal weapons obscure which fighter controls each.
lessons.cause: Similar paths and overlapping arm shapes weaken ownership.
lessons.intervention: Shorten the knight counterthrust and give it a distinct path; keep the skeleton diagonal.
lessons.preserve: Preserve both grips and the central shield response to the ninja.
lessons.limit: The revised knight blade has little visible area and still needs scrutiny. This is a partial repair, not a model of finished combat anatomy.
lessons.probe: Name the owner of each weapon without selecting its part. If labels are needed, the read is unresolved.
